parsed_output.answer: The acid-and-leaf experiment is used to model how the stomach is protected from its own acid. In this experiment, two similar green leaves are taken. One leaf is coated with petroleum jelly or vaseline, while the other is left untreated. A weak acid is then applied to both leaves. After some time, it is observed that the leaf without petroleum jelly is damaged by the acid, while the leaf coated with petroleum jelly remains unaffected. This is because the petroleum jelly acts like the mucus lining of the stomach, which protects the stomach walls from the corrosive effects of stomach acid. The mucus lining in the stomach serves a similar function, forming a protective barrier that prevents the acid from damaging the stomach walls.
